P7480.corridor_notes: GEM's 'Duyun Branch Pipeline' (都匀支线, 33.9 km) is a spur of the multi-branch Guizhou branch-pipeline network (贵州天然气支线管网项目) that fans out from the China-Myanmar/West-East trunk near Guiyang. A tender notice for geological-hazard inspection of the network (bbda.com; www.dlnyzb.com/detail/28463843) explicitly lists '中缅天然气管道都匀支线长34km' alongside a 522 km main trunk and shorter Yunwu/Dushan/Libo spurs — corroborating the branch's existence and length (GEM: 33.90 km). A separate bid notice for capacity-upgrade work at '贵阳输油气分公司都匀支线都匀输气站' confirms the branch terminates at Duyun Gas Transmission Station in Duyun City. The network's shared origin point is 燕楼门站/燕楼分输站 (Yanlou gate/distribution station) in Yanlou Town, Huaxi District, Guiyang — matching GEM's existing StartLocation exactly (EIA notices: 燕楼镇位于花溪区西南部, 距花溪城中心14公里, 距省会城市贵阳市中心27公里; 燕楼分输站 design pressure 6.3 MPa, design annual throughput 6.1×10^8 m3/a). Public sources describe the shared Guiyang–Huishui–Changshun corridor and the individual named spurs (Duyun, Dushan, Libo, Yunwu, Duyun–Kaili) but do not pinpoint the exact km-post where the 34 km Duyun spur physically diverges from that shared corridor toward Duyun city — so the sourced start point here is the network's shared Yanlou origin (consistent with GEM's own field), not a verified mid-corridor branch point.
P7480.researcher_notes: GEM's existing StartLocation 'Yanlou Town, Huaxi District' independently confirmed (Yanlou gate/distribution station, EIA acceptance notices). EndLocation (previously null) resolved to Duyun Gas Transmission Station via a Baidu tender-bidding listing for capacity-upgrade work at that exact station under the 都匀支线 name, and the branch's 34 km length corroborated by a separate geological-hazard-survey tender covering the whole Guizhou network (matches GEM's 33.90 km closely). Note: a different, unrelated project also uses '都匀' in its name — a Duyun-Kaili local distribution spur (都匀至凯里) operated by Kunlun Gas's 都凯分公司 — ruled out as not matching (different operator/scope, not part of the China-Myanmar trunk network).
P7480.blockers: The precise geographic point where the 34 km Duyun spur diverges from the shared Guiyang-area corridor (vs. simply starting at the shared Yanlou hub, as used here) is not documented in any source found; treated as low materiality since GEM's own StartLocation already specifies Yanlou.
